messages:
maria: Heads up — got a burst of OOMs on dedicated-prod after last night's runtime merge (commit f3a9c2). Affected nodes: gpu-pool-12.* :alarm_clock:

aj: Can you paste the most recent logs? CI green before merge?

maria: CI perf looked fine but prod shows memory fragmentation + repeated slab compactions. Logs:
```
[2026-03-18T01:12:08Z] kv_slab: compacter took 186ms, freed 0 pages
[2026-03-18T01:12:09Z] slab_alloc: allocation failed, OOM after 2GB used
[2026-03-18T01:12:09Z] kernel_router: pinned thread 11 -> cpu3
```

aj: Noted. CI bot shows a perf regression around kernel-thread-pinning and slab-aging change set. @ci-bot link?

ci-bot: CI perf: https://ci.redwood/example/9876 — autobench shows +18% mem-alloc p90 and 12% throughput drop on longctx tests.

devon: I ran a quick pprof on a repro VM. Allocation flamegraph suggests the compacter isn't merging small free ranges; fragmentation grows with sequence length. Snapshot top:
```
pprof: top 10 allocs
40.2%  runtime.mcachealloc
22.7%  runtime.Sweep
18.5%  kv.slab.free_range_scan
8.1%   kernel.router.select_kernels
```

kai: That aligns with the kernel-selector change I landed — it pins the compactor thread to reduce eviction jitter. Looks like on high-seqlen loads the compactor gets starved or serializes with the allocator, increasing fragmentation.

maria: Repro script (small):
```
for i in {1..200}; do ./client --prompt "<very long prompt>" --batch 16; done
```
Produces progressive OOM within ~60s on a node with 48GB.

aj: Can we toggle the new slab-aging heuristic at runtime to validate? IIRC there's a flag: `--slab-aging=enabled|disabled` in the agent config.

kai: Yes. Quick test patch to fallback to previous behavior if fragmentation > 30%:
```
- if (slab_age_factor > 0.6) pin_compactor();
+ if (slab_age_factor > 0.6 && frag_ratio < 0.3) pin_compactor();
```
I can push a hotfix to canary.

devon: Also tried disabling pinning manually — compactor spreads across CPUs, fragmentation reduced in flamegraph, throughput restored in my VM. So likely interaction between pinning + longctx heavy batches.

maria: This is blocking the rollout for the release train. Ops wants rollback if canary hits prod.

aj: Let's bisect to be sure there's no secondary change. Steps: 1) rollback pinning change in canary 2) run the repro 3) if fixed, merge revert; if not, continue bisect. I'll take 1.

kai: I'll prepare a revert PR for the pinning commit and a toggle flag for slab-aging. Also adding a guard to prevent compactor pin when avg-seq-len > 1024.

sre-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-451. Assigned to eng-runtime oncall.

maria: Thanks. Plan: canary revert now, run repro, if green promote. If not, full rollback. Assigning follow-ups: @aj will run bisect, @kai will open revert + toggle PR, @devon will collect full pprof traces for next 2h. :thumbsup:

aj: On it — will report back in 30m with canary results.
